Brew Notes Guides

How do you choose a pour-over dripper?

By Sam Rivera · October 1, 2026

Pick a dripper by material and size: ceramic holds heat best, glass shows the brew, and metal is the most durable. A size 02 dripper suits one to four cups, which covers most kitchens.

Which material is best?

MaterialHeatDurability
CeramicBestGood
GlassGoodFair
MetalFairBest

Ceramic drippers need to be preheated with hot water, but once warm they keep the brewing temperature steady. Glass is lighter and lets you watch the coffee bed. Metal drippers are nearly unbreakable, which makes them a good choice for travel or camping trips. Plastic drippers are cheap and also hold heat well, though some people prefer to avoid plastic with hot liquids. Whatever you choose, look for a stable base and a hole size that matches the grind you plan to use, since that controls how fast water flows through the coffee.

What size should you buy?

  • Size 01: one or two cups.
  • Size 02: one to four cups.
  • Size 03: three to six cups.

Most people brew one or two cups at a time, so a size 02 gives you flexibility without wasting filters. If you regularly make coffee for guests, size 03 saves you a second brew. Check that the dripper sits securely on your favorite mug, because some wide drippers wobble on narrow cups. Filters are sized to match, so buy the same number as your dripper. Paper filters give a clean cup, while metal and cloth filters let more oils through for a fuller body. Rinse paper filters before brewing to remove any papery taste and to preheat everything.

FAQ

Do I need a gooseneck kettle?

It helps you pour slowly, but any kettle works if you pour gently.

How fine should I grind?

Medium-fine, like table salt, is a good start.
